claimed_purpose.text: A self-organizing, Zettelkasten-inspired dynamic memory system for LLM agents that eschews rigid schemas in favor of flexible, content-driven organization
Designed for coding agents; memories organize into a Zettelkasten-style graph with dynamic relationships
Persistent retrieval to facilitate sharing of memory from multiple agents across sessions
Implements concepts from academic paper on agentic memory for LLM agents
LLMController is used for memory metadata generation

mechanisms.text: Collections are created via get_or_create_collection; the distance metric (defaulting to L2 instead of cosine) is set at collection creation time and cannot be changed afterward, requiring export-delete-recreate-reimport to migrate existing persistent stores

The bug can cause a memory's content field to describe one entity (e.g. Apartment/Convenient Store) while its context and tags become overwritten with unrelated data (e.g. Hospital-related), a direct continuity corruption.

When a new memory is added, the system generates comprehensive notes, creates contextual descriptions and tags, analyzes historical memories for relevant connections, and establishes meaningful links.
Notes are persisted in two stores simultaneously: an in-process dict (self.memories) and ChromaDB (via ChromaRetriever). Both are updated on every add, update, and delete operation.
Retrieval uses self.retriever.search(query, k) called at least twice in the same code path, potentially intended to use different embedding retrieval methods at each call site.
When a new note is added, the system can alter contextual representations or metadata in existing notes by querying the LLM, supporting evolution of the knowledge graph
All memory operations including summarization, linking, and evolution are performed by the LLM itself, avoiding hand-crafted workflows or static graph operations
A-MEM exposes an `add` method that accepts a summary string and tags including agent_id and session_id, indicating per-agent and per-session isolation metadata.
Each memory note is a structured tuple capturing content, time, LLM-generated keywords/tags/context, dense embedding, and links
Two-phase retrieve policy: breadth-first metadata peek, then depth-first drill into specific memories to minimize token usage
Agents write memories by explicitly calling A-MEM memory APIs during a session; no call means nothing is stored.
Project-specific isolation stores memory in ./chroma_db; global option shares across projects via CHROMA_DB_PATH
The memory vector interface encompasses insert, update, delete, search, and metadata handling operations
Session-start hook scaffolds the model to use memory tools at the start of each session
ChromaDB provides persistent vector embedding storage backing the memory store.
Delete removes the note from both ChromaDB and the in-memory dict.
Retrieved memories can be filtered or re-ranked by score threshold
Embedding model is configurable; default is all-MiniLM-L6-v2

ledger.claim: A bug causes degraded semantic retrieval quality in A-MEM because collections default to L2 distance rather than cosine, mismatching the embedding model's training objective
ledger.quote: All ChromaDB collections are created without specifying a distance metric, so they default to L2 (squared Euclidean). Sentence embedding models (including the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 used here) are trained to produce vectors where cosine similarity is the meaningful distance measure. Using L2 treats vector magnitude as significant when it isn't, producing lower-quality nearest-neighbour retrieval.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Retrieve failure: a semantic query will not match a memory whose relevant terms appear only in LLM-extracted tags, not in the raw content string — the LLM's extraction work is wasted at search time.
ledger.quote: This means a query like `"ollama GPU setup"` won't match a memory whose content is `"NVIDIA driver 590.48.01 is compatible with kernel 6.17"` even though it has tags `["ollama", "gpu", "nvidia"]`. The LLM's extraction work is wasted at search time.
ledger.label: inferred
